title: Cheapest Smallest Mirror Word
statement:
You get a lowercase string s. In one step you may overwrite any single character with any lowercase letter.

Turn s into a palindrome (a string that reads the same backwards) using the fewest steps. If several palindromes need that same fewest number of steps, return the one that comes first in dictionary order.

examples.why: Two mirrored pairs differ: b/d and r/a. Each needs one change, and keeping the smaller letter (b, then a) gives the earliest string.
It is already a palindrome. "aaaa" is smaller, but it costs four steps instead of zero.
One step is required. Changing c to a beats changing a to c.

constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters
hints: Positions i and n − 1 − i must end up equal. Do different pairs affect each other?
Each mismatched pair costs at least one step, and one step is always enough for it. So the count of steps is fixed; only the chosen letters vary.
For a mismatched pair, overwrite the larger letter with the smaller one. Any other choice either costs an extra step or makes the string bigger.

explain.intuition:
A palindrome only links position i with its mirror n − 1 − i. Pairs are independent, so you can decide each pair on its own. A matching pair costs nothing and should be left alone; changing it would add a step. A mismatched pair costs exactly one step: rewrite one side to match the other.

Which side? The two choices produce the same cost, and the result differs only in that pair's letter. The smaller letter makes the whole string smaller, because the left copy of the pair comes before anything decided later at a larger index. So always copy the smaller letter onto both sides.
steps: Put i at the start and j at the end.
While i < j, set both a[i] and a[j] to min(a[i], a[j]), then move both pointers inward.
Join the array and return it.
pitfalls: Making every character a for the smallest string. That breaks the fewest-steps rule, as "noon" shows.
Always copying the left letter onto the right side. In "dcba" that gives "dccd", not "abba".
Building the result with repeated string concatenation in a loop over a long input; use an array and join once.

solutions.title: Two pointers, keep the smaller letter
solutions.idea: Walk inward from both ends. For each mirrored pair, write the smaller letter on both sides.

solutions.title: Build the left half and mirror it
solutions.idea: The answer is fixed by its left half (plus the middle character for odd lengths). Build that half from pairwise minima, then append its reverse.

followups: Each letter change now costs the alphabet distance between the old and new letter. What is the cheapest palindrome?
You may make at most k changes and want the smallest string, palindrome or not. How does the greedy change?
